title: GeneralCovarianceReverseFisher.lean

problem_class.label: nonconvex
problem_class.details: Unconstrained optimization of reverse Fisher divergence over n Gaussian-mixture means in R^d. The student has equal weights and shared covariance Σ = AA*, and the target is N(μ*, Σ). This mixture parameterization permits nonconvex objectives.

oracle.label: exact_gradient
oracle.details: Each call returns the full Euclidean gradient of the population reverse Fisher loss with respect to all n means, exactly for every history and seed. Gaussian integration is internal to the oracle; samples and target scores are not separately available.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: The parameter space is the Euclidean product (R^d)^n, with positive integers d = dimension and n = components.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: The shared covariance is arbitrary positive definite with lower·I ≼ Σ ≼ upper·I and 0 < lower ≤ upper. Its root A and the target mean μ* are hidden. Public information comprises d, n, lower, upper, radius R ≥ 0, accuracy ε > 0, and initial means satisfying max_i ||start_i − μ*|| ≤ R. Allowed algorithms use positive scalar gradient-descent steps from these initial means and output the current iterate.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/GeneralCovarianceReverseFisher.lean: Params, Model, spectralBounds, startBound, gdFamily, spec.publicInput, spec.valid, spec.allowedAlgorithm.

accuracy.label: distance_to_solution
accuracy.details: The final output must satisfy max_i ||θ_i − μ*||² ≤ ε, where ε = accuracy; every mixture component must recover the same target mean.

accuracy.label: deterministic
accuracy.details: The guarantee holds for every algorithm and oracle seed realization, including probability-zero realizations, under the fixed extracted oracle budget.
accuracy.evidence: LongTails/Setups/GeneralCovarianceReverseFisher.lean: spec.successful universally quantifies ω; LongTails/Template.lean: Convergence, execute.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: A specialized population reverse-Fisher optimization problem with hidden shared general covariance, exact full-gradient access, scalar gradient-descent restrictions, and simultaneous componentwise parameter recovery. No qualifying reference was verified; this does not establish novelty. Local proofs and implementations were not inspected.

descriptionHtml:
Reverse Fisher Gradient Descent

We study gradient descent on the reverse Fisher loss F between an equally weighted Gaussian mixture with m≥1 means in Rd, d≥1, and a Gaussian target with mean x⋆∈Rd. Both share an unknown covariance Σ satisfying λ−I⪯Σ⪯λ+I, where 0<λ−≤λ+. The loss averages the squared Euclidean difference of their log-density gradients under the mixture. Each given initial mean θi0 lies within distance R≥0 of x⋆. The oracle returns ∇F(θ) at θ. For ε>0, the final means must satisfy ∥θ¯i−x⋆∥2≤ε for every component and every realization of algorithm randomness.

Write E=(Rd)m, equipped with the product inner product and norm ∥θ∥E2=∑i=1m∥θi∥2. The model consists of an invertible linear map A:Rd→Rd and the target mean x⋆, with Σ=AA⊤. Define the unnormalized log densities hθ(x)=log⁡(∑i=1mexp⁡(−∥A−1(x−θi)∥22)),h⋆(x)=−∥A−1(x−x⋆)∥22. Their gradients with respect to x equal the corresponding log-density gradients. For Z∼N(0,Id), define F(θ)=1m∑ℓ=1mE[‖∇hθ(θℓ+AZ)−∇h⋆(θℓ+AZ)‖2]. The optimization problem is minθ∈EF(θ). The algorithm receives d,m,λ−,λ+,R,ε, and θ0∈E; A and x⋆ are accessible only through the oracle.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Covariance bounds). For every v∈Rd, λ−∥v∥2≤∥A⊤v∥2≤λ+∥v∥2.

Assumption 2 (Initial localization). The given initial means satisfy ∥θi0−x⋆∥≤R,i=1,…,m.

Our formulation is algorithm-specific: we analyze gradient descent with positive, potentially adaptive step sizes. Queries may be made at any point of E, and ∇F denotes the gradient under its product inner product. Starting from the given θ0, each oracle call and update have the form gt=∇F(θt),θt+1=θt−ηtgt,ηt>0. The step size is selected from the algorithm’s current information before receiving gt and may depend on its randomness. The expectation defining F is part of the objective; oracle replies are exact gradients of that objective.

After K oracle calls, the output is the last iterate θ¯=θK. The required accuracy is ∥θ¯i−x⋆∥2≤ε,i=1,…,m, for every realization of the algorithm’s randomness.

comparisonHtml:
An equal-weight mixture pθ=n−1∑i=1nN(θi,Σ) fits a single teacher q=N(μ¯,Σ) in Rd, with n,d≥1, 0<sminI⪯Σ⪯smaxI and maxi∥θi0−μ¯∥≤R. The oracle returns the exact full gradient of L(θ)=∫∥∇xlog⁡pθ−∇xlog⁡q∥2pθ(x)dx. The setup requires positive-step GD from the supplied initialization and its last iterate; the target is maxi∥θiK−μ¯∥2≤ε, deterministically, for ε>0.

Reverse Fisher GD with general shared covariance: GeneralCovarianceReverseFisher.
Result Oracle complexity Novelty Limitations
(1) GeneralCovarianceReverseFisherGD (Ours) (review) O(1+(1+log⁡n)κ2⋅[log⁡(1+R2/smin)+nmin{n,d}smax/ε])
(2) GD (Tyurin 2026), Thm. 2.1, Cor. 2.5; rescaled to Σ=σ2I O(1+(1+log⁡n)⋅[log⁡(1+nR2/ε)+nmin{n,d}σ2/ε]) (1): Scope extends GD analysis to arbitrary SPD covariance, with κ2 overhead. At Σ=σ2I, matches known rate; improves constants and removes the redundant accuracy logarithm from the initialization term.
(3) Derived bound: collapsed means, conjugate gradients (Hestenes and Stiefel 1952), §3 O(d+1) exact-gradient calls, including initialization; exact recovery. Same problem and oracle, without the GD-family restriction. (1): Analyzes GD from arbitrary supplied means; no established problem-class complexity improvement. (1): Polynomial ε−1 cost versus finite exact recovery. Needs spectral bounds and R for its budget; (3) needs neither, nor ε.

Abbr: n: student components; d: dimension; smin,smax: covariance spectral bounds; κ=smax/smin; R: initial radius; ε: squared-distance tolerance; σ2: isotropic covariance scale; GD: gradient descent; SPD: symmetric positive definite. Costs count full population-gradient calls in exact arithmetic.

Hestenes, Magnus R., and Eduard Stiefel. 1952. “Methods of Conjugate Gradients for Solving Linear Systems.” Journal of Research of the National Bureau of Standards 49 (6): 409–36. https://doi.org/10.6028/jres.049.044.
Tyurin, Alexander. 2026. Global Convergence of Gradient Descent for Score Matching in Gaussian Mixtures via Reverse Fisher Divergence. https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2606.19876.

import LongTails.Template
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Gradient.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Adjoint
import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.PiL2
import Mathlib.Probability.Distributions.Gaussian.Multivariate

open MeasureTheory OracleTemplate
open scoped RealInnerProductSpace

namespace LongTails.Setups.GeneralCovarianceReverseFisher

structure Params where
  dimension : ℕ+
  components : ℕ+
  lower : ℝ
  upper : ℝ
  radius : ℝ
  accuracy : ℝ
  start : Fin components → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin dimension)

abbrev Space (p : Params) := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin p.dimension)

abbrev Means (p : Params) := PiLp 2 (fun _ : Fin p.components => Space p)

structure Model (p : Params) where
  covarianceRoot : Space p ≃L[ℝ] Space p
  target : Space p

noncomputable def logMixture {p : Params} {k : ℕ} (A : Space p ≃L[ℝ] Space p)
    (centers : Fin k → Space p) (x : Space p) : ℝ :=
  Real.log (∑ i, Real.exp (-‖A.symm (x - centers i)‖ ^ 2 / 2))

noncomputable def loss {p : Params} (M : Model p) (θ : Means p) : ℝ :=
  (∑ ℓ, ∫ z, ‖gradient (logMixture M.covarianceRoot (fun i => θ i)) (θ ℓ + M.covarianceRoot z) -
      gradient (logMixture M.covarianceRoot (fun _ : Fin 1 => M.target))
        (θ ℓ + M.covarianceRoot z)‖ ^ 2 ∂ProbabilityTheory.stdGaussian (Space p)) /
    p.components

def spectralBounds (p : Params) (M : Model p) : Prop :=
  ∀ v, p.lower * ‖v‖ ^ 2 ≤ ‖ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint
      (M.covarianceRoot : Space p →L[ℝ] Space p) v‖ ^ 2 ∧
    ‖ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint (M.covarianceRoot : Space p →L[ℝ] Space p) v‖ ^ 2 ≤
      p.upper * ‖v‖ ^ 2

def startBound (p : Params) (M : Model p) : Prop :=
  ∀ i, ‖p.start i - M.target‖ ≤ p.radius

def gdFamily (p : Params) (A : Algorithm (Means p) (Means p) (Means p)) : Prop :=
  ∃ (point : A.State → Means p) (step : A.State → ℝ),
    (∀ state, 0 < step state) ∧
    (∀ seed, point (A.initial seed) = WithLp.toLp 2 p.start) ∧
    (∀ state, A.query state = (0, point state)) ∧
    (∀ state reply, point (A.update state reply) = point state - step state • reply) ∧
    (∀ state, A.output state = point state)

noncomputable def spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Params
  Instance := Model
  Query := Means
  Reply := Means
  Output := Means
  publicInput := id
  valid p := 0 < p.lower ∧ p.lower ≤ p.upper ∧ 0 ≤ p.radius ∧ 0 < p.accuracy
  admissible p M oracle := spectralBounds p M ∧ startBound p M ∧
    ∀ k query seed, oracle.answer k query seed = gradient (loss M) query.2
  successful p M output _ := ∀ ω i, ‖output ω i - M.target‖ ^ 2 ≤ p.accuracy
  allowedAlgorithm := gdFamily

end LongTails.Setups.GeneralCovarianceReverseFisher
